interest: Shows 1930 State Department guidance on Japanese imperial court dress rules for American women.
keywords: Division of International Conferences and Protocol
overview: Correspondence (1930): State advises an American woman on Japanese court dress - afternoon wear for private audiences, evening dress with a four-yard train for the New Year's Reception.

people.name: Richard Southgate
people.role: Assistant Chief, Division of International Conferences and Protocol

subfiles.about: Inquiry from Rosalind Gluck requesting information on appropriate dress and train regulations for American women presented at the Japanese Court.
subfiles.summary: Rosalind Gluck asks State for the dress and train-length rules for women presented at Japan's Imperial Court.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rosalind Gluck to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Court dress regulations

subfiles.about: Official reply detailing the attire and four-yard train requirements for foreign women attending private audiences and formal receptions at the Japanese Court.
subfiles.from: Richard Southgate (Assistant Chief, Division of International Conferences and Protocol)
subfiles.summary: Southgate tells Gluck Japan requires afternoon dress for private audiences, and evening dress with a four-yard train for state events.
subfiles.title: Letter from Richard Southgate to Rosalind Gluck regarding Japanese Court dress regulations
